subject.title: [Bug]: Subagents can appear completed before the underlying delegated work is actually finished

question: Should child-owned background exec/process sessions block subagent completion, or should they remain separate active work surfaced through task/session status?
rationale: Current code has two valid boundaries: subagent completion follows the child agent-run result, while long-running exec/process sessions are separately registered and pollable; choosing which state owns user-visible completion affects timeout, cancellation, and detached-job semantics.

options.title: Keep completion agent-run authoritative
options.body: Subagent completion stays tied to the child agent turn, but any child-owned running process must remain visible in `/tasks`, `session_status`, or final handoff text so users do not see a false all-done state.

options.title: Block completion on owned processes
options.body: Subagent finalization waits for child-owned process sessions to finish, with explicit timeout, cancel, cleanup, and tests to avoid indefinite completion hangs.

options.title: Require live repro first
options.body: Hold implementation until a focused live reproduction captures the exact UI/status path and process ownership state that appears completed too early.

recommendation.title: Keep completion agent-run authoritative
recommendation.body: Subagent completion stays tied to the child agent turn, but any child-owned running process must remain visible in `/tasks`, `session_status`, or final handoff text so users do not see a false all-done state.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest related history is in subagent announce and descendant-gating code that defines when parent completion is emitted.
